criteria: Splits the work into separate stages for at least: loading the order, checking it is not empty, computing the amounts, and charging (not one or two stages doing everything)
All stages share one error type: a union with a discriminant field (such as tag or code) per failure, including the missing order and the empty order
Returns the missing order and the empty order as left values instead of throwing
The initial context holds only orderId and couponCode; it does not set the stages' outputs to placeholder values such as 0, null, [] or an empty order
Each stage adds its output by returning a new object spread from the context it received

scenarios.prompt: Using groucho-fp, our ticket-triage flow is loaded at runtime from the `./triage` folder, one stage per TypeScript file, run in this order: classify the ticket, detect its language, pick a team, assign an agent, notify the agent. We expect to add stages between existing ones later. All stages share one context type and one error type, and two of them use a `normalizeText(text: string): string` helper. Show the project layout with the file names, then write the 'pick a team' stage file for the context `{ ticketId: string; text: string; category?: string; language?: string; team?: string; agentId?: string }`.
criteria: The stage file names start with numeric prefixes that sort in the run order: classify, language, team, assign, notify
The prefixes are zero-padded or of equal width (for example 10-, 20-, 30- or 010-, 020-), so alphabetical order is the run order
Leaves gaps between the prefixes (for example 10, 20, 30) so a stage can be added between two others without renaming files
The shared types and the normalizeText helper are outside the ./triage folder, or the loader is given a pattern that matches only the stage files
The team stage file imports the shared context and error types (for example from ../types) instead of declaring its own copies
The lowercased text is no longer written over the text an earlier stage wrote: it goes to a new key, or trimming and lowercasing are done in one stage that writes text once
The tokenize stage returns a context that still has raw (it spreads ctx without removing keys)
The defaults stage no longer replaces meta with a new object: it keeps the meta reference it received, writes the defaults to a new key, or is removed
Does not fix the run by making the conflict hook accept every conflict
